title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: On Monday a student finishes a chat with your assistant and says she will book the CNC router on Thursday. On Thursday she opens a brand-new chat. Nothing was saved anywhere. What does the model know about Monday?

options.text: Everything, because the model stores each chat it has had
Only a summary, which the model writes by itself at the end
Nothing, because each new call starts with only its own input
Everything, as long as the chat fits inside the context window

items.stem: A run has three model calls. The first call's input is 2,000 tokens. Each tool result adds 1,000 tokens to the history, and the program re-sends the whole history on every call (ignore the model's own output). Calls 2 and 3 each follow one tool result. How many input tokens are paid for across the three calls in total?
Your assistant must answer from a 400-page set of machine manuals. Which approach best fits a small model budget?

options.text: Paste all manuals into the system prompt, so every answer has the facts
Search the manuals per question and add only the best few passages
Ask the model to recall the manuals from its training, to avoid tokens
Save the manuals as notes, so the model remembers them between sessions

items.stem: In one or two sentences: your team wants the assistant to remember each student's training status between visits. What must the program do, and when, for this to work?

A teammate proposes switching to a model with a much larger context window so the assistant will not need any notes. In one or two sentences, why does this not solve the problem of remembering students between visits?
